stories.title: Delta to begin rolling out free trans-Pacific Wi-Fi this month
stories.summary: Delta says it has received regulatory approval to extend free Delta Sync Wi-Fi, presented by T-Mobile, to its trans-Pacific routes. The rollout is scheduled to begin later this month and to expand progressively across routes in the following weeks. Delta says the expansion would complete free Wi-Fi coverage across its global network, which it describes as spanning six continents.
paragraphs: Delta has cleared the regulatory step needed to bring its free onboard internet to trans-Pacific flying. The airline says the rollout of Delta Sync Wi-Fi, presented by T-Mobile, will start later this month and then spread route by route over the following weeks rather than switching on everywhere at once.

Delta frames the Pacific as the last major gap in its connectivity map. The airline says nearly 1,300 of its aircraft — more than 95% of the fleet — are already equipped, and that once the Pacific routes are activated it would be the only U.S. global carrier offering free Wi-Fi across a network spanning six continents. That claim is Delta's own characterization of its network.
keyPoints: Rollout begins later this month and expands progressively across trans-Pacific routes in the following weeks.
Nearly 1,300 Delta aircraft, more than 95% of the fleet, already have Wi-Fi installed.
Wi-Fi is free and presented by T-Mobile, per Delta; activation timing will vary by route.
stories.takeaway: If you have a Delta trans-Pacific flight coming up, treat Wi-Fi as route-dependent rather than guaranteed on day one — availability should arrive progressively over the following weeks, so check your flight's onboard amenities closer to departure.

stories.title: Timing matters when applying for Delta American Express cards
stories.summary: The Points Guy reports that because American Express generally limits cardmembers to one welcome bonus per card per lifetime, the timing of a Delta American Express application carries weight. The article frames the decision around when a prospective applicant should apply rather than which card is best. No specific welcome offers, spending requirements or deadlines are supported by the candidate text, so those details are not stated here.
paragraphs: The Points Guy published guidance arguing that applicants should think carefully about when, not just whether, to apply for a Delta American Express card. The stated reason is that American Express generally restricts cardmembers to one welcome bonus per card per lifetime, which the publisher treats as the key constraint on timing.

Because no fetched evidence accompanies this candidate, the specific offers, minimum spending requirements, annual fees, eligibility limits and deadlines are not verified and are not reproduced. Readers who want current terms should confirm them directly with American Express before applying.
keyPoints: The Points Guy frames the article around when to apply for a Delta American Express card.
The publisher cites American Express's one-welcome-bonus-per-lifetime limit as the reason timing matters.
stories.takeaway: Before applying for a Delta American Express card, check the current welcome offer terms on the issuer's own page and confirm you can meet any minimum spending requirement during the offer window, since American Express generally allows only one welcome bonus per card per lifetime.
